sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.10619 of 2025
Order:

This writ petition has been filed seeking to declare the action of respondent Nos.2 to 4 in not disposing of their representation dated 15.10.2022 nor restoring the possession of the subject land to the individual assigned patta holders and making any compensation to the petitioners as per the settled law, as illegal and arbitrary and for other appropriate reliefs.

It is stated that the petitioners were granted assignment pattas in respect of Acs.3.00 each in Survey No.289 of Jalaram Revenue Village, Ramgiri Mandal, Peddapally District, in the year 1992 and since then they have been cultivating the said lands.

It is further stated that pattadar pass books and title deeds were also issued in favour of the petitioners in respect of the said lands and they are receiving various incentives being sanctioned by the Government for cultivation of the same.

The grievance of the petitioners is that despite the same, the respondent No.5 herein i.e., Singareni Collieries Company acquired the said lands and forcefully dispossessed them, without issuing any notice and without following any procedure for payment of compensation as prescribed under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which constrained the petitioners to submit several representations on the file of respondent Nos.2 to 4, but so far no action has been taken thereon.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government for Revenue appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4 has disputed the issuance of assignment pattas in favour of the petitioners in respect of the subject land, by stating that the petitioners have not produced any original pattas much less they are in possession of the original pattadar pass books alleged to have been issued in their favour in respect of the said land.
He further submits that in fact, the entries in the Dharani portal would show the name of respondent No.5 as pattadar of the subject land.

Since it appears that there are disputes with regard to right, title and nature of the subject lands, this Court, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition by directing respondent No.4 to conduct enquiry into the matter and if it is found that the pattas alleged to have been issued in favour of the petitioners are genuine and the said lands have been acquired by respondent No.5, he shall submit a report on the file of respondent No.2 for initiating appropriate proceedings for payment of compensation to the petitioners under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The writ petition is accordingly disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
